'''Jillsarians''' were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of muscular [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] with four [[Limb/Legends|arms]]<ref name="Cracken's Rebel Operatives" /> from the [[Jillsaria system/Legends|Jillsaria system]].<ref name="EAOC" /><ref name="Planetnamia" /> Their integument varied, with some individuals possessing [[orange]] skin<ref name="The Lost Prince" /> while others were covered in [[brown]] fur.<ref name="Cracken's Rebel Operatives" />

[[Golben]], a technician onboard ''[[Omze's Incredible Traveling Starport/Legends|Omze's Incredible Traveling Starport]]'' was a Jillsarian,<ref name="Platt's Starport Guide" /> as was [[Resik (Jillsarian)|Resik]], a bartender on [[Reuss VIII/Legends|Reuss VIII]] who went on to become an [[operative]] for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]].<ref name="Cracken's Rebel Operatives" /> [[Doodnik Sharpelz]], owner of [[Doodnik's Café]] on [[Tyne's Horky]], was a Jillsarian who spent his formative years on [[Ojom/Legends|Ojom]], [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of another four-armed species, the [[Besalisk/Legends|Besalisks]].<ref name="The Droids Re-Animated">{{SW|url=news/the-droids-re-animated-part-2|series=The Droids Re-Animated|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref> Jillsarians were also known to live on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="Mos Eisley">''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Jillsarians first officially appeared in the guise of Resik, a character in [[1994]]'s ''[[Cracken's Rebel Operatives]]'', a [[roleplaying game]] supplement for [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition]]''. Another Jillsarian, Golben, appeared the following year in that company's ''[[Platt's Starport Guide]]''.

[[File:Fourfistsinyourface.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Doodnik Sharpelz]]
However, two previously existing four-armed characters were long suspected of being Jillsarian. An unidentified four-armed background character appeared in an illustration in ''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]'' in [[1993]]. More prominently, the four-armed [[Chef/Legends|chef]] Doodnik first appeared as the owner of [[Doodnik's Café]] in "[[The Lost Prince]]," a [[1985]] episode of the [[Star Wars: Droids: The Adventures of R2-D2 and C-3PO|''Star Wars Droids'']] animated television series. While [[Gregory Walker]]'s [[2009]] work "[[Dining at Dex's]]" hinted at Doodnik being a Besalisk by making him hail from their homeworld of Ojom, Walker acknowledged that the explicit identification was not actually made.<ref name="Walker">{{JCFCite|url=posts/30656900|board=Literature|thread=Hyperspace New Short Fiction: "Dining at Dex's" & Xim Week & new Alex Winger story now online!|user=[[Gregory Walker|NarbFlick]]|date=2009-12-30|time=5:00 AM}}</ref> This left the door open for the second part of [[Abel G. Peña]] and [[Rich Handley]]'s [[StarWars.com|Official Star Wars Blog]] post, "[[The Droids Re-Animated]]," to address the uncertainty in [[2013]], making Doodnik a Jillsarian who had grown up on Ojom.<ref name="The Droids Re-Animated" />
